transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (CTO, AtlasText), Evan Morales (Lead ML Eng), Rana Ahmed (Product), Jordan Lee (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): discuss quickstart credits, hosted API TTFT, dedicated/private fit for PII, security docs, schedule benchmark.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, account lead for this region, with Liam from our SE team. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya (CTO): Hi Maya, Priya here. Thanks — excited to see what you offer.
[00:09] Evan (AtlasText): Evan here, lead on the ML infra.
[00:11] Rana (Product): Rana, product.
[00:13] Jordan (SRE): Jordan, SRE.
[00:15] Liam (Redwood SE): Hey, Liam — focus on performance/benchmarks and private deploys.
[00:18] Maya: Great. Agenda — quickstart credits and how long to first token, hosted vs dedicated vs private fit for sensitive docs, security/compliance items, and then next steps with a benchmark. Anything else to add?
[00:29] Priya: No that's perfect. For context we are shipping a document summarization feature that will hit PII sometimes, and we need to understand where Redwood fits and the fastest path to prototype.
[00:38] Evan: Also curious on latency at 1–2 qps, 10–20 seq len mostly but sometimes 512 tokens for long docs. Cost targets matter too.
[00:46] Maya: Understood. Quickstart first — we do PLG self-serve: you can sign up and get a small free credit pool, but for pilots we usually provision additional credits. TTFT for a simple hosted API call is typically under 5 minutes from sign-up to first token if you use our SDK/CLI and the quickstart guide.
[01:05] Jordan: Under five minutes? That seems optimistic — do you mean assuming we've already whitelisted IPs and SSO?
[01:09] Liam: Good clarifying Q. For a standard developer flow, no SSO or private network, it's just account creation, API key in the console, and a simple curl/SDK call — that path is designed to be minutes. If you require VPC peering or private control plane, TTFT can be 1–2 days depending on networking and approvals, but we can accelerate for pilots.
[01:30] Priya: Our compliance team will likely demand VPC peering and customer-managed keys for PII — so likely Private or Dedicated.
[01:37] Maya: Yeah, many customers start on Hosted to validate product and then move to Dedicated or Private for isolation. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable latency; Private gives you customer-managed networking and KMS integration.
[01:50] Evan: Can you clarify the difference on latency between Hosted and Dedicated for the same model? We need p95 under 400ms for short prompts ideally.
[01:58] Liam: Hosted is multi-tenant with optimized routing; typical p95 for small models is 200–600ms depending on load and model. Dedicated can be tightly provisioned and hit the lower bound — p95s around 150–300ms sustained. The big lever is batching and KV cache behavior for repeated prefixes.
[02:16] Rana: You mentioned KV cache — will that work out-of-the-box? Any instrumentation we need?
[02:20] Liam: We have built-in KV/prefix caching and automatic continuous batching. For initial tests, you don't need extra infra. We'll instrument traces in the console so you can see token-level latency and cost breakdowns.
[02:32] Priya: Security: do you have SOC2, ISO? Where do audit logs live and can we route them to our SIEM?
[02:38] Maya: We are SOC2 compliant; ISO in progress. Audit logs are available in the Console and can be streamed to S3 or delivered via our log-forwarder to Splunk/Datadog. For Private deployments you can keep audit logs on-prem.
[02:52] Jordan: KMS — we need CMEK/HSM integration. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:56] Liam: Yes, for Private we integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options). For Dedicated we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS depending on contract. Hosted offers provider-managed keys by default.
[03:09] Evan: Let's talk pricing for pilot scale — say 10k tokens/day average, with spikes. How do credits map to cost?
[03:15] Maya: We'll send a sample pricing matrix; credits are effectively prepaid USD against usage. For pilots we provision a credit bucket so teams can just call the API without billing friction. If you go Dedicated we offer reserved capacity pricing which is cheaper per token at scale.
[03:28] Priya: Can you demo the sign-up flow? We mostly want to know the developer experience and what to expect from our SRE side.
[03:34] Liam: Quick walkthrough: sign-up -> Console -> API keys -> SDK examples. If you want, we can do a short live where I create an API key and run a simple summarize call.
[03:41] Priya: That would be helpful.
[03:43] [03:44] Liam: (screen share voice) Okay I won't share screen in the transcript but the steps are — console redwood.consolee...oh sorry, Redwood Console, top-right create api key, copy, then run curl -X POST to /v1/generate with prompt.
[03:58] [04:00] Evan: Any gotchas around network egress for hosted? We have strict firewall rules and outbound whitelisting to only a few endpoints.
[04:06] Maya: Hosted endpoints are public; you can restrict keys and IPs with per-key allow-lists. For stricter environments, Private with VPC peering is recommended.
[04:15] Jordan: How does VPC peering work? Are we peering to a managed VPC?
[04:19] Liam: For Private, we deploy a customer-specific control plane in your VPC or set up secure peering. There is some network setup on both sides — usually 1–3 business days if networking teams are responsive. We also support transit gateways for large enterprises.
[04:35] Priya: From a project timeline: we'd like a prototype in 2 weeks, pilot in 6–8. Does Redwood have a self-serve path that aligns with that?
[04:44] Maya: Yes — if you accept hosted quickstart we can have a prototype in days. If you need Private, the TTFT is longer but we can parallelize: provision hosted credits for devs while we start the Private networking. Many customers do both in parallel.
[04:58] Rana: About models — do you host open models or proprietary ones? Any quantization/accuracy tradeoffs?
[05:04] Liam: We support a catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified configs. We recommend quantized variants for cost/throughput tradeoffs; we surface quality regressions in Optimize and provide eval tooling. For QA-sensitive flows use the full precision variant on Dedicated/Private; for high-throughput non-sensitive flows quantized models can save 40–70% cost.
[05:25] Evan: Benchmarks — can you run workload that simulates our patterns? We'll share prompt set and sequence length distribution.
[05:31] Maya: Absolutely. Action: Evan/Priya send prompts and traffic shape; Liam will set up the benchmark bench harness and run on Hosted and Dedicated fixtures.
[05:40] Priya: Any limitations on embedding vectors or rate limiting we should know for production?
[05:44] Maya: Hosted has per-account rate limits that scale; Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and configurable autoscaling policies. For embeddings we can allocate more parallel GPU capacity.
[05:55] Jordan: Data retention — hosted stores inputs for 30 days by default?
[06:00] Liam: We store logs/inputs per your settings. For Hosted customers who choose not to opt-in, we do not retain user data beyond short diagnostic windows; we can toggle retention and for Private/Dedicated you control retention policies.
[06:15] Priya: Regarding SSO — we use Okta. Can we use SAML/SCIM?
[06:19] Maya: Yes, SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning are supported across Console. We'll send a quick SSO setup guide.
[06:27] Evan: Competitor Q: some of our folks like Anthropic's model family for summarization — how does Redwood play with different model types?
[06:34] Liam: We can serve many architectures and provide migration guidance. If you want Anthropic-style models, we can host compatible open variants or integrate vendor endpoints via routing policies. Redwood's differentiation is the serving runtime and observability across choices.
[06:52] Priya: For compliance we need pen-test reports and SOC2 — can you share those?
[06:56] Maya: Yes, we'll email the security pack — SOC2 report, pen-test summary, architecture diagram showing Private options, and KMS integration notes.
[07:05] Rana: On rollouts — if we deploy model changes how do you support canary/A-B and fallbacks?
[07:10] Liam: Redwood Console supports canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants with weighted traffic. We also track quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
[07:20] Priya: Great. Let's talk tempo: who owns the benchmark run and timeline?
[07:25] Maya: Action items — I'll provision a 10K credit bucket and share account link; Liam will create the benchmark config; Evan/Priya to send prompts and traffic. We'll aim to run the benchmark next week.
[07:36] Jordan: Do you have any sample infra as code or Terraform for private deploys?
[07:40] Liam: We have Terraform modules and an architecture repo to share. I'll attach that in the follow-up.
[07:48] Priya: One last tricky: our legal wants to know about data residency — we have EU customers, any EU region support?
[07:54] Maya: Yes, Redwood has EU regions and can pin deployments. For Private you can host entirely in your region. We'll capture residency requirements in the follow-up.
[08:06] Evan: Are there ways to pre-warm KV caches for common doc prefixes?
[08:10] Liam: You can prefill cache with recent contexts and we have APIs for prefix hints. That reduces cold-start tail latency.
[08:17] Priya: Okay this is helpful. Recap and next steps please.
[08:20] Maya: Recap — Redwood will: 1) provision credits and share signup link, 2) send security pack (SOC2, SSO setup, KMS notes, pen-test), 3) Liam will create benchmark harness and run hosted+dedi fixtures, 4) schedule an hour-long benchmark next week, 5) provide Terraform modules and private deploy docs.
[08:40] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side? Evan/Priya to send prompt set and traffic distribution; Jordan will review network constraints for peering.
[08:48] Maya: Perfect. Any other questions?
[08:50] Rana: None from Product.
[08:52] Evan: No. Thanks.
[08:54] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pack and credits.

(End of recording)
